notes.title: The Philosophy of Lusst’ghaa
notes.notes:
[i]The most merciful thing in the world, I think, is the inability of the human mind to correlate all its contents. We live on a placid island of ignorance in the midst of black seas of infinity, and it was not meant that we should voyage far. The sciences, each straining in its own direction, have hitherto harmed us little; but some day the piecing together of dissociated knowledge will open up such terrifying vistas of reality, and of our frightful position therein, that we shall either go mad from the revelation or flee from the light into the peace and safety of a new dark age.[/i]
                                                                                                                                         ~H.P. Lovecraft

Hello there, Cultists! 

The quote above is the opening lines of Call of Cthulhu, probably the most famous of Lovecraft’s works. It says about how remaining ignorant about the true nature of reality is a blessing. How about you? How many of you have wondered what exactly are the rules governing the otherworldly dimension present in Lust from Beyond? It is a fascinating, if disturbing, place. Let’s see how much we know about it.

The first and most obvious thing about Lusst’ghaa is its otherworldliness. We’ve tried to achieve that feeling of foreignness with our worldbuilding and plot. The story of Lusst’ghaa is truly tragic, more so because its current state wasn’t caused by evil intent. There are motivations in play that we’d perhaps empathize with if we were allowed to explore them, and that’s what makes this world terrifying, just like Lovecraft’s stories.

The one omnipresent theme is that of pain and pleasure, which are not only not mutually exclusive but rather codependent. In Lusst’ghaa there is no pleasure without pain and vice versa. They are so closely related to one another that there comes a point where they are indistinguishable. 

Lusst’ghaa operates on rules beyond human understanding. There is a hierarchy of gods, and their affairs are way above our understanding. A human being is in comparison completely insignificant. Just like in Lovecraft’s works, we’re mere observers. Humans mean nothing to these foreign powers, they might see our world but don’t concern themselves with individuals. If you walk down the street and step on a bug, you didn’t do it to kill, you probably won’t even notice, but for that bug, it’s the matter of life and death. And it’s the same here. The powers governing Lusst’ghaa are perhaps not entirely malicious, at least from their perspective – but if fate says so, they might cause our destruction.

Perhaps it is for the better that we don't know more about Lusst’ghaa. After all, to paraphrase Lovecraft, ignorance is bliss.

notes.title: FAQ: What is the M Edition?
notes.notes:
Hi, Cultists!

We’ve seen your questions about the upcoming M Edition, and we are here to answer them all. Reveal what awaits beyond reality!

[b]Q: Is Lust From Beyond: M Edition a completely new game?[/b]
A: It is a new version of Lust from Beyond. It’s a game with the same story and gameplay, but with less focus on the explicit content.

[b]Q: Why did you make this version of the game?[/b]
A: We’ve put a lot of heart into our game and we wanted to enable more gamers to play it. By default, Adult Only games are unavailable in some markets, like Germany and China. They are also hidden on Steam to everyone unless you manually enable Adult Only titles in your settings. 

Besides, Lust from Beyond isn’t gratuitous. Its elements serve to tell the story and invoke certain feelings or thoughts in the players. At heart, it’s a Lovecraftian horror touching upon themes like curiosity, physicality or lust. It’s an immersive story-driven survival horror first, with explicit parts being a cherry on top. It can easily stand on its own without the most extreme elements, so we decided to make it more accessible for the players who look for a more subtle experience. 

However, you’ll still find plenty of horror visuals in it!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34600191/8242449b493e86f1c07904bf7aa8f49f629c1fcd.png[/img]

[b]Q: What is the difference between Lust From Beyond and the M Edition?[/b]
A: There are a couple of differences.
Nudity and explicit sexual content have been reduced. Example: private parts are tastefully covered by a piece of clothing (that’s still very much cultish and aligned with the themes of the game). 
Some scenes have been rearranged to keep their meaning but reduce the explicit factor. Example: an orgy became a ritual cult meeting.
Some animations, scene framing and models have been changed to meet the Mature rating requirements instead of Adult Only.

[b]Q: What does M stand for? [/b]
A: M means the M (Mature) rating, but there’s more to it! At first, we wanted to call it Masked Edition, since we tastefully covered some of the elements of the game. Also, Amanda’s mask is one of the most visually distinct elements of our world. But we went for M, because it’s such an appropriate letter. It stands for Mask, Mystery, Mature... It sounded just right.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34600191/7337077628f00acabdac23c2b5eba843c7e2536f.png[/img]

[b]Q: Which version of Lust from Beyond should I play?[/b]
A: They are the same game, just presented slightly differently. If you like horror for the mystery, narrative and atmosphere, but don’t care that much for extremely shocking images, then the M Edition is the right choice. It’s what you’d expect from a strong horror game. If you like your horror as hardcore as possible, then you can try the unrated version of the game.

We hope this shines more light on what’s to come. Lust from Beyond: M Edition is a dark horror that will take you beyond reality. See you in Lusst’ghaa!

If you’d like to support us, please add our game to your Wishlist https://store.steampowered.com/app/1641890/Lust_from_Beyond_M_Edition/

notes.title: The imagination of one has inspired so many.
notes.notes:
Cultists, let’s take a moment to appreciate Howard Philips Lovecraft, the writer whose stories and poems had a great influence on the Lust universe.

He excelled at sowing fear into the hearts of readers by facing them with the otherworldly and incomprehensible beings and concepts. 

The entire story of Lust from Beyond is heavily inspired by Lovecraft, but our biggest tribute to the writer is the chapter called Shadow Over Bleakmoor. You might recognize it immediately as a reference to Shadow Over Innsmouth, one of Howard’s most iconic stories.

The rooftop chase is directly influenced by the short story, and it’s also our nod to Call of Cthulhu: Dark Corners of the Earth, an older Lovecraftian game that we appreciate very much.

[previewyoutube=LqB5egn4eDg;full][/previewyoutube]

Enjoy this fragment of the chase in Lust from Beyond: M Edition, and follow us for the full experience.

notes.title: Book Recommendations from Beyond
notes.notes:
[h3]Hi there, Cultists![/h3]
For some time now we’ve been sharing our weekly reading recommendations with our fans on [url=https://discord.gg/3GxnHEX7md]Discord[/url], [url=https://twitter.com/MGLunarium]Twitter[/url] and [url=https://www.facebook.com/LustFromBeyond]Facebook[/url]. We’d like to share them here with you as well. The stories below have inspired us greatly, and we hope you’ll like them as well. Enjoy!


[h2]The King in Yellow[/h2]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34600191/279cbbaee8e158267a8f0b89daa16f1f57fba7b4.jpg[/img]

This is where esoteric horror really started. Chambers’s tales, focused around a book that inspired madness, had a huge influence on Lovecraft. They also were referenced heavily in the first season of True Detective. It’s A MUST-READ!

[h2]Providence[/h2]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34600191/056f421eecea6fb3e6b20e7f67ba2de5d0750ba4.jpg[/img]

Not just any Providence. Alan Moore’s PROVIDENCE! It’s a highly controversial graphic novel that orbits around H.P. Lovecraft and his mythos. If you dig the lore, every page is chock full of references. It’s also a complex, compelling and at times shocking story that intertwines with Moore’s two other books. But, we’ll let you discover that for yourself.

[h2]The Murders in the Rue Morgue[/h2]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34600191/4ba7fafad7a2ab572dc845d396d0ec91da3b0058.jpg[/img]

Looking for a mystery dripping with atmosphere? Then you just have to pick up Edgar Allan Poe's The Murders in the Rue Morgue. Or rather all Poe's stories about Dupin, who was basically a different version of Sherlock Holmes. There's gore, there are dark secrets, and... we just feel you're gonna like it.


Did you like any of the books we recommended? Review them in the comments or share your recommendations!

notes.title: An erotic Lovecraft game has been funded on Kickstarter
notes.notes:
Lust from Beyond looks like Amnesia with giant alien vaginas. It's an erotic first-person horror romp inspired by the likes of Lovecraft and Giger, with a horny cult trying to open a door to a sex dimension. Typical cult stuff. Expect puzzles, corridors that look like xenomorph nests, and quivering, sentient cocks. Check out the Kickstarter trailer above. It's a bit NSFW. 

As a Victorian antiquarian plagued by visions of the aforementioned sex dimension, you decide to join the Cult of Ecstasy to figure out what's going on with your weird dreams. The cult seems to know how to have a good time, namely with orgies, but when that's not enough they decide to open the door to Cthulhu's sex pad. 

Though evocative of Amnesia, you'll actually be able to fight the monsters chasing you through the vagina tunnels, though you can still try to hide from them. I'm sure they just want a cuddle, though. 

Lust from Beyond is a standalone game, but it's also a sequel to Lust for Darkness, which had a nearly identical premise. A guy goes to a Victorian mansion and then finds himself hanging out in the same alien dimension we'll be visiting again. It looked interesting but James ended up just finding it childish. 

Such a juvenile, shallow fascination with sex makes Lust for Darkness hard to take seriously from the start. It fails to even attempt to explore the horrors of sexual trauma, anxiety, or taboos. Instead it banks on a simple apprehension with Doing It™ and the organs involved to get a rise out of its players, but its clumsy arrangement of story, themes, puzzles, and stealth are as flaccid and unfinished as I am right now.

The sequel was funded on Kickstarter in only ten days, though the developer was only looking for £8,000. Backers will get an exclusive demo within 24 hours, but there's no release date yet. The Steam page says "coming soon".
